segments.text: [soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Place the flame near eye level and sit comfortably. Blink whenever needed, and stop for pain, dizziness, excessive tearing, or lasting eye discomfort.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [soft distant winter wind] Let the flame become one warm ember resting in a wide field of snow. Keep the gaze gentle rather than rigid.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice the blue near the wick, the gold above it, and the soft halo around the edges.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Blink naturally. Each time the eyes reopen, meet the ember without trying to pin it in place.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Allow attention to rest on the quiet contrast between warmth and darkness.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Close your eyes. Notice any after-image floating behind the eyelids like an ember beneath snow.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Let the image change colour, move, fade, or disappear. There is nothing to preserve.
[soft, slow, warm voice] If no image appears, rest with the dark field itself and feel the body breathing.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Allow the eye muscles to soften completely.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Open the eyes and return to the flame. Notice movement without losing the centre.
[soft, slow, warm voice] The ember leans and rises, never holding one shape for long.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Stay with colour and light while allowing easy blinks.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Let the wide dark room support the small bright point.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Close your eyes again. Watch the remembered ember or the simple darkness where it had been.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Feel forehead, cheeks, jaw, and eyes becoming quiet as snow.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Widen to the whole body and the sounds around you.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Open your eyes slowly. Leave the ember in the flame and carry only the steadiness.
